title: Restore installed scoring generics with development S7
description:
Installed filtro examples and vignettes cannot call `fit()` with development S7 because method registration leaves an external-generic sentinel in its reexported binding. Run the S7 build hook after registration to restore the imported generic. Keep the hook conditional for released S7 0.2.2, and quote the score-class vector defaults so class creation remains warning-free.

Use S7’s load, unload, and build hooks when available, retaining `methods_register()` for older releases. On development S7, unloading removes the package’s external S7 methods and dependency hooks, and the build hook cleans external generic bindings after method declarations.

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to filtro website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the filtro website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: handle transformation of single or multiple score v2
description:
Enable `transform = TRUE` for both 

- `fill_safe_value()` 
- `fill_safe_values()`.

Usage 

- If user set `transform = TRUE` in `fill_save_value()`, all objects (all predictor columns) are transformed, identity-transformed or not. 
- If user set `transform = TRUE` in `fill_save_values()`, all objects (all predictor columns) are transformed, identity-transformed or not. 
- Currently, all score objects use the identity transformation, except for the correlation score object, which uses the absolute transformation, and for ROC AUC score object, which uses the pmax, i.e., `max(x, 1 - x)`, transformation.

Replace PR [#174](https://github.com/tidymodels/filtro/pull/174)

Close #155 
Close #156 
Close #176

title: handle transformation of single or multiple score
description:
Close #155 
Close #156 

` transform_score()`

- Take in a tibble or data frame returned by `fill_safe_values()`.
- Return a tibble or data frame with column(s) whose values transformed based on the transformation function passed in.


``` r
class_score_list |> fill_safe_values()
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   outcome    predictor    aov_pval cor_pearson    imp_rf infogain
#>   <chr>      <chr>           <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 Sale_Price MS_SubClass    237.         1     0.0148     0.266  
#> 2 Sale_Price MS_Zoning      130.         1     0.00997    0.113  
#> 3 Sale_Price Lot_Frontage   Inf          0.165 0.00668    0.146  
#> 4 Sale_Price Lot_Area       Inf          0.255 0.0137     0.140  
#> 5 Sale_Price Street           5.75       1     0.0000455  0.00365

class_score_list |>
  fill_safe_values() |>
  # Change some values to negative for demonstration
  dplyr::mutate(
    cor_pearson = replace(cor_pearson, 1:2, -1)
  ) |>
  transform_score(trans = list(cor_pearson = abs))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   outcome    predictor    aov_pval cor_pearson    imp_rf infogain
#>   <chr>      <chr>           <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 Sale_Price MS_SubClass    237.         1     0.0148     0.266  
#> 2 Sale_Price MS_Zoning      130.         1     0.00997    0.113  
#> 3 Sale_Price Lot_Frontage   Inf          0.165 0.00668    0.146  
#> 4 Sale_Price Lot_Area       Inf          0.255 0.0137     0.140  
#> 5 Sale_Price Street           5.75       1     0.0000455  0.00365

class_score_list |>
  fill_safe_values() |>
  transform_score(trans = list(cor_pearson = function(x) pmax(x, 1 - x)))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   outcome    predictor    aov_pval cor_pearson    imp_rf infogain
#>   <chr>      <chr>           <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 Sale_Price MS_SubClass    237.         1     0.0148     0.266  
#> 2 Sale_Price MS_Zoning      130.         1     0.00997    0.113  
#> 3 Sale_Price Lot_Frontage   Inf          0.835 0.00668    0.146  
#> 4 Sale_Price Lot_Area       Inf          0.745 0.0137     0.140  
#> 5 Sale_Price Street           5.75       1     0.0000455  0.00365

class_score_list |>
  fill_safe_values() |>
  # Change some values to negative for demonstration
  dplyr::mutate(
    cor_pearson = replace(cor_pearson, 1:2, -1),
    imp_rf = replace(imp_rf, 1:2, -imp_rf[1:2])
  ) |>
  transform_score(trans = list(cor_pearson = abs, imp_rf = abs))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   outcome    predictor    aov_pval cor_pearson    imp_rf infogain
#>   <chr>      <chr>           <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 Sale_Price MS_SubClass    237.         1     0.0148     0.266  
#> 2 Sale_Price MS_Zoning      130.         1     0.00997    0.113  
#> 3 Sale_Price Lot_Frontage   Inf          0.165 0.00668    0.146  
#> 4 Sale_Price Lot_Area       Inf          0.255 0.0137     0.140  
#> 5 Sale_Price Street           5.75       1     0.0000455  0.00365
```

title: Review documentations for constructor.R & score-aov.R
description:
Would like to get some feedback before documenting other function(s) or if any of these function(s) needs any modification prior to documenting. 

This PR submits the following documentations for review: 

constructor.R

- `new_score_obj`

score-aov.R

- `score_aov`
- `get_scores_aov`

Additional notes: 

- `@param trans`. Haven't decided to what do to with it. 
- `@param sorts`. Reserved for sorting functions _after_ the score result is computed. Some of the options are: `identity, abs, max(score, 1 - score)`. 
- `@param neg_log10`. Optional argument to turn the negative log10 transformation off. Because it is not an attribute of the score object, it is documented using `@details`,  if that is okay?  e.g., 

```
  score_obj = score_aov()
  score_obj$score_type <- "pval"
  score_obj$neg_log10 <- FALSE # Turn -log10() off
  score_res <- get_scores_aov(score_obj, data, outcome)
```

- Random forest method also have similar optional arguments, e.g., `engine, trees, mtry, min_n` are not attributes of the score object

```
  score_obj <- score_forest_imp()
  score_obj$engine <- "ranger" 
  score_obj$trees <- 10
  score_obj$mtry <- 2
  score_obj$min_n <- 1
  score_obj$class <- TRUE # TODO
  set.seed(42)
  score_res <- get_scores_forest_importance(score_obj, data, outcome)
```

title: Review S3method (bind_scores() and fill_safe_values()) in utilities.R
description:
This PR submits the following functions for review:

In `utilities.R`

- `bind_scores`:  Bind all metadata `score_obj` and score result `score_res`, and assign class `score_set` to combined scores.
- `fill_safe_values`: Fill in safe values. The safe value (`fallback_val`) is specific to `score_obj`. 

NOTE
- example (folder `inst` > `example_ames.R`) shows exampled API usage 


For example: 

Create score object based on aov (anova fstat), cor (correlation), and imp (random forest importance) 

```
# ANOVA F-statistic
score_obj_aov <- score_aov()
score_res_aov <- get_scores_aov(score_obj_aov, data, outcome)
score_obj_aov <- score_obj_aov |> attach_score(score_res_aov)

# Correlation
score_obj_cor <- score_cor()
score_res_cor <- get_scores_cor(score_obj_cor, data, outcome)
score_obj_cor <- score_obj_cor |> attach_score(score_res_cor)

# Random forest importance 
score_obj_imp <- score_forest_imp()
score_obj_imp$engine <- "ranger"
score_obj_imp$trees <- 10
score_obj_imp$mtry <- 2
score_obj_imp$min_n <- 1
score_obj_imp$class <- FALSE # TODO
set.seed(42)
score_res_imp <- get_scores_forest_importance(score_obj_imp, data, outcome)
score_obj_imp <- score_obj_imp |> attach_score(score_res_imp)
```

Create a list of score objects 
`score_obj_list <- list(score_obj_aov, score_obj_cor, score_obj_imp) `

Bind scores

```
> score_obj_list |> bind_scores()
# A tibble: 5 × 5
  outcome    predictor    fstat pearson      imp_rf
  <chr>      <chr>        <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>
1 Sale_Price MS_SubClass   64.0  NA     2459280908.
2 Sale_Price MS_Zoning     63.8  NA     1031493890.
3 Sale_Price Lot_Frontage  NA     0.202 1791146274.
4 Sale_Price Lot_Area      NA     0.267 2832934188.
5 Sale_Price Street        10.4  NA        2626742.
```

Fill in safe values, i.e., `NA` for `fstat` is filled with `Inf` (safe value). `NA` for `pearson` is filled with `1` (safe value). 

```
> score_obj_list |> fill_safe_values()
# A tibble: 5 × 5
  outcome    predictor    fstat pearson      imp_rf
  <chr>      <chr>        <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>
1 Sale_Price MS_SubClass   64.0   1     2459280908.
2 Sale_Price MS_Zoning     63.8   1     1031493890.
3 Sale_Price Lot_Frontage Inf     0.202 1791146274.
4 Sale_Price Lot_Area     Inf     0.267 2832934188.
5 Sale_Price Street        10.4   1        2626742.

```
